Commentary.Commentary: The two skippers and the umpires are having a chat! We are moments away from this game being called off we believe. Just as I write that, the two captains shake hands which means the game has been abandoned. We believe we were quite lucky to even have the amount of cricket we witnessed today as it was a total downpour earlier on. After the toss, it kept raining and we had a delay close to 3 hours. However, despite all of that, the groundsmen did a brilliant job and got us all set for a 9-over per side game. We did see first of those 9 overs but just as the innings ended, the rain returned and then the inevitable happened, the game was called off. Now this becomes a three game T20I series with the second one being played on the 31st of this month. That game will begin on 1100 local (1500 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

The second innings should have begun by now but that is not the case as the rain is still coming down. Covers are on. Difficult to see this game getting underway again. Well Russell is still not in his whites so that probably gives an indication that they do not expect this rain to pass quickly.

Now then, the target is not a big one but it is not going to be easy to chase one this wicket! Windies have a good bowling side and Pakistan will need to start well. A good second passage awaits but first, we will have to wait for the rain to pass.

The Pakistan bowling was good but there were quite a few boundary balls! However, Hasan Ali was superb. Usman Qadir and Shadab Khan too were good. Shaheen and Wasim though were a little expensive. Yes, 10 per over in a 9 over game might seem fine but the wicket is a good one for the bowlers so it will be considered expensive.

Pollard walks off with a smile! However, as he walks off, the rain comes down and so do the covers! However, that was 9 good overs of cricket but one has to believe Windies have got a good score as this is not the easiest of wickets to bat on. The hosts kept losing wickets at regular intervals but they kept hitting boundaries too. None of their batters made a huge contribution but everybody played a part. Their skipper though was the star for them with an excellent innings.

SIX! That is not where you should be bowling to Pollard at this stage. Afridi bowls a length delivery on middle, right in the arc of Pollard. He turns and pulls it over deep square leg for a biggie. Good end to the innings as WEST INDIES FINISH ON 85/5.
In the air, but safe! On a length on middle, Kieron Pollard pulls it towards mid-wicket. It lands safely and Pollard takes two comfortably.
FOUR! Pollard gets it right this time! Bangs a short ball on middle, Kieron Pollard is up for the challenge and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Very well bowled! Short of a length on off, Kieron Pollard looks to pull but misses.
It looks like Kieron Pollard has some issue with his bat. Change of bat for him. Let's see what he can do with his new bat in the last 4 deliveries.
A low full toss on middle, a slower one. Holder chips it to the vacant square leg region for a single.
Good length ball on off, Holder swings his blade hard but only to connect it with thin air around him. Good start from Shaheen Afridi.
Shaheen Afridi to bowl the final over.
A single to end! On middle, this is hit over the bowler's end. Not off the middle and one is taken.
Another dot! Gold at this stage! Length and around off, this one jags back in. Holder looks to push it on the off side but gets hit on the glove.
Jason Holder walks out to bat at No.7.

OUT! TAKEN! Hasan Ali has another one! This is a superb delivery! It is short and it is another slower one. Hetmyer looks to pull but the ball hits the splice and lobs towards the keeper where Mohammad Rizwan takes an easy catch. Pakistan have done well so far to keep picking wickets at regular intervals.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Rizwan b Hasan Ali

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and around off, this is guided towards point for one.

Two more! Pollard had to hurry there! Had Hasan collected the ball, Pollard was a goner! A short one, on middle, Pollard looks to pull, it is a slower one so he is a touch early. It goes off the top edge and over fine leg. Pollard takes one and goes for the second. He is struggling a little. The throw comes in towards the keeper's end where Hasan goes but he does not collect the throw. Pollard would have been out.

SIX! Powered! That is against the wind and it goes all the way! Perfect start to the over. This is angled into the batter, seems like a slower one, it is heaved over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Back of a length ball on middle, Hetmyer looks to cut it away but misses. After 7 overs, West Indies are 62/4.
FOUR! Connects it sweetly this time! On a length on middle, Shimron Hetmyer opens the face of the bat and creams it through covers for a boundary.
Slower delivery outside off, Shimron Hetmyer looks to paddle scoop it over the keeper's head but fails to connect.
Length ball on off, Pollard guides it to third man for a single.
FIVE WIDES! That is poor from Wasim! Sprays it way down the leg side. Beats everyone to the fine leg fence.
On a length on off, Hetmyer taps it to point for a single.

OUT! TAKEN! Mohammad Wasim gets rid of a big fish here! The Universe Boss has to walk back! Good length ball on middle, Chris Gayle makes room for himself and gets hold of this one as he lifts it to long on. But didn't get the elevation he was looking for and Hasan Ali pouches it. A maiden wicket for Mohammad Wasim and that also of whom. He is pumped.
Commentary.Howout: c Hasan Ali b Mohammad Wasim

Commentary.Commentary: Mohammad Wasim is back into the attack. He conceded 9 in his first over.
The googly, it lands on middle and then turns back in. Pollard looks to flick but misses.
Kieron Pollard is the new batsman in.
Review time! Andre Russell have taken a review for a caught behind. Ultra Edge confirms there is a spike as the ball passes the bat. The original decision stays. Russell is OUT!

OUT! THERE IS A SPIKE AS THE BALL PASSES THE EDGE! Russell walks back and he takes a review along! Huge wicket with three overs to go. Usman bowls this full and outside off. Russell looks to go over covers, there is a noise as the ball goes past the bat. The keeper takes it and appeals. The finger is raised. Russell reviews, Almost immediately. Replays show that the on-field call is the right one.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Rizwan b Usman Qadir

Commentary.Commentary: Another dot! Quicker and outside off, this is slapped but to covers.
Good comeback! Drags his length back and bowls a leg spinner outside off, Russell looks to hit across the line but misses.
SIX! Over the fence. Russell joins the action now! That is brute power! It is a dipping full toss around off, he gets under it and lofts it well over the cover fence. 50 up.
Flatter and outside off, this is guided to point.
SIX! Gets too close to Gayle and that has been put away! Tossed up nicely and on off, Gayle smashes it well over the long on fence for a biggie. The last ball spoils the over.
Flatter and outside off, once again this one comes slow off the surface. Gayle hits it back to the bowler.
Gayle had to get back in quickly! Shorter and outside off, Gayle looks to slap it hard but it goes off the inner half back to the bowler.
Flatter and on the pads, this is worked through square leg for one.
Just the one! On middle, this is pulled down to long on for one.
Extra bounce! That really sticks in the surface too! Shorter and outside off, Gayle looks to pull but is early in the shot. He misses.
Andre Russell walks out to bat! Also, Shadab Khan to have a go.

OUT! TAKEN! Good comeback from the experienced Mohammad Hafeez! Tossed it up on middle, Nicholas Pooran stays deep in the crease and looks to heave it over extra but miscues it. He ends up slicing it towards backward point. Shadab Khan settles under it and takes it with ease.
Commentary.Howout: c Shadab Khan b Mohammad Hafeez

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! OUT OF HERE! Floated it up on middle, Nicholas Pooran moves across, gets under it and smashes it over deep mid-wicket for six more runs. He is such a good player of spin. Bring out a new ball please!
Short and on leg, Nicholas Pooran looks to reverse sweep it but misses. He gets hit on the thigh pad.
Slower through the air around off, turns further away. Pooran swings his blade but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Loopy ball outside off, Pooran leaves it alone.
SIX! BANG! Tossed up on middle, Nicholas Pooran makes enough room for himself and hammers it over the bowler's head for a maximum.
Time for some spin now! Mohammad Hafeez is brought into the attack.
A quick run to end! Fuller and on off, this is pushed to mid off for one. A wicket in the over but runs too.
FOUR LEG BYES AGAIN! Not good from Hasa Ali! He once again drifts down the leg side, Pooran looks to flick again but misses. It hits the pad and goes down to the fine leg fence.
FOUR! Leg byes! Windies won't mind how they come as long as they do! This is shorter and on the pads, Pooran looks to heave it, misses and this hits the pad and goes down to the fine leg fence.
Another beauty! This lands on off, it is a back of a length ball, holds its line. Pooran is beaten as he tries to block.
Another lovely slower one, this is shorter, Pooran looks to defend but is hit high on the glove.
Nicholas Pooran is the new batsman in.

OUT! 50th T20I wicket for Ali in his 50th T20I and that too on his first ball of the game! What a slower one, what a slower one. It just does not come out better than this. Wow! Lewis has been done in, in pace totally. It is fuller, Lewis does not pick it, in the end he tries to play a check-shot, ends up chipping it to mid on. Afridi takes a dolly. Big wicket as Lewis is probably the most dangerous Windies batter.
Commentary.Howout: c Shaheen Afridi b Hasan Ali

Commentary.Commentary: Hasan Ali comes into the attack. He replaces Shaheen Afridi.
Good length and around off, moves away a little. Gayle plays it late and to short third man. Despite two boudaries, it was a good over by Wasim.
The physio is out and Simmons is seen walk off the field. Rightly so. Gayle walks out to bat.
That is nasty! That was quick! A short one and on the body, Simmons is taken by surprise, he looks to pull but misses to get hit on the body. He is down on the ground straightaway. Not good.
FOUR! Up and over! A lot of width on offer, it is short and outside off, Simmons carves it over point for a boundary.
In the air... safe! A slower one outside off, just sticks in a surface a little. Lewis looks to hit it over the off side but ends up splicing it towards deep cover. One taken.
Half an appeal! Fuller and on middle, Lewis looks to flick, he gets an inside edge onto the pads.

EDGY FOUR! Welcome to international cricket! A full ball to begin with, it is outside off. Lewis swings, it goes off the outside edge down to the third man fence. That though was a forutnate boundary but it is not the line you want to bowl to Lewis.
Mohammad Wasim to bowl from the other end.
Full ball, on off. Pushed to mid off. Just 7 from the first over!
Short ball, around leg. Simmons looks to pull but gets no bat on it. Wide called as it went over his head.
FOUR! First boundary! Length ball, on middle. Simmons gets the inner half of the bat as he looks to heave it. The ball runs past short fine leg and runs to the fence.
Swing and a miss! Length ball, outside off. Simmons looks to heave it to the leg side but gets no bat on it.
Off the mark! On the pads, Lewis clips it to deep square leg for one.
First runs! Full ball, outside off. Simmons drives it to mid off for a quick single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
Good length ball, outside off. Left alone by Simmons.
We are set for the action!! The Pakistan fielders walk out in the middle. Evin Lewis and Lendl Simmons walk out to bat for West Indies. Shaheen Afridi to start with the ball.

Hayden Walsh is down for a chat. He says that they have good confidence from playing against the Aussies. Adds that he has learned to stay patient and sticking to his plans. Mentions that the focus has been on T20's and the transition to the ODI format was tougher. Adds that he will look to be consistent and stick to the plans.

Shadab Khan is down for a chat. He says that the England tour was a tough one but they learned a lot from it. Adds that experience of playing in the West Indies in the CPL and for Pakistan helps them. Says that it is special to play his 50th T20I today and he thanks God and his family. Mentions that he has been working on his bowling and he did quite well in England.
Update 1235 Local (1635 GMT) - We have a match on our hands! Yes, the umpires have decided that the game will resume at 1245 Local. It will be a 9-over match and the first 3 overs will be Powerplay!

Update 1230 Local (1630 GMT) - The covers are off! I repeat the covers are off! The umpires are out in the middle and the ground staff is hard at work currently. The Pakistani players are busy playing some football on the sidelines. Well at least some of them are. We hope for more updates soon! The umpires are having a quick chat with Kieron Pollard and Babar Azam.

Update 1145 Local (1545 GMT) - The rain has abated a bit but the drizzle is still on, it is still quite gloomy out there though. The umpires are out there but umbrellas aren't completely necessary now. We have already started losing overs now. Just a reminder that 1316 Local is the latest when a 5-over game can start. We hope that it doesn't come to that and we get some more action soon!
Update 1038 Local (1438 GMT) - Uh oh! This is not a good sign. The rain has gotten heavier now and it has gotten really dark too. The ground staff call for more covers!
Update 1020 Local (1420 GMT) - The rain seems to have gone now as the umpires walk out to have a look without the umbrella. The covers are still firmly placed as there are dark clouds hovering above.

Ian Bishop was spot on! The drizzle has passed us, the players are out for the National Anthems and we are not far away from the first ball. First, the national anthem for Barbados will be played followed by Pakistan's national anthem. In the end, West Indies' cricket anthem, "Rally 'round the West Indies", is played. But hold on, the drizzle returns as the anthems end and the players head back to the dressing room. We are in for another delay folks!

Rain, rain everywhere at the moment! The covers are on in the Women's 100 and the covers are on here too as there is a slight drizzle. Ian Bishop reckons it should not be a long delay and we too hope for the same. It seems to be the slightest of drizzle as the players are not in shelter, the Windies players at least.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Lendl Simmons, Evin Lewis, Chris Gayle, Shimron Hetmyer, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Kieron Pollard (C), Andre Russell, Dwayne Bravo, Hayden Walsh, Akeal Hosein, Sheldon Cottrell.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Sharjeel Khan, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Hafeez, Fakhar Zaman, Azam Khan, Shadab Khan, Hasan Ali, Mohammad Wasim, Shaheen Afridi, Usman Qadir.
Toss - The news from the middle is that Pakistan have won the toss and they will bowl first!
Breaking news - Moments before the toss, we have some news from the Pakistani camp and it is that Mohammad Wasim is going to make his International debut in this game!

This game could very well come down to the battle between West Indies' batting and Pakistan's bowling. Yes, the hosts have done quite well with the ball in the last couple of series but historically, it is their muscle with the bat that has overshadowed their bowling. Coming to the tourists, they often find their bowling department with the responsibility to win them games. It is not because they lack talent with the bat, but primarily due to lack of consistency. This is why one feels that this contest would come down to have the batters from the Caribbean and Pakistan's bowling fare against each other. Well, no matter what happens, it is quite likely that a lip-smacking clash awaits us!

Hello and a very warm welcome to the first T20I between West Indies and Pakistan. We have gotten plenty of exciting T20 action in international cricket in the last couple of months and this series promises to be no different. Both these teams are coming off of contrasting results in their last T20I series and with the World Cup coming up, both would be keen to cross the T's and dot the I's as far as their squads for the mega tournament is concerned. Who will get off to a winning start in the 4-match series? We will find out. Stay tuned for toss and more updates.
